summary_student.text: This was a computer study that used data from fuel droplets burned on the International Space Station in the FLEX experiment. It simulated 'cool flames', very weak flames around a burning droplet, and how gentle heating or drifting air makes them flicker, turn into hot flames, or go out. The record says this could improve fire-safety models for spacecraft.

summary_professional.text: Ground investigation building a 3-D OpenFOAM CFD model of n-alkane droplet cool flames in microgravity, coupling variable-density Navier-Stokes flow with low-temperature chemistry, heat and mass transfer and radiation, validated against ISS FLEX measurements. Simulations imposed convection alone (droplet drift), heat flux, and combined convection plus heating on large (1–4 mm) and sub-millimeter (~0.5 mm) droplets, sweeping forcing amplitude and frequency, ambient composition (including ozone-assisted cases) and pressure. Extracted observables were ignition delay, oscillation frequency and amplitude, and stand-off and extinction diameters, used to build stability maps for cool-flame onset, persistence and quenching.

pillar.reason: The record states the work could improve spacecraft fire-safety modeling by resolving cool-flame and extinction behavior and help define safer operating envelopes and materials.
